segments: 213 Constantine his brother alone, three years.
Now he was pleasant and noble-spirited.
And when he died,
he delivered the kingdom to his nephew,
whose name was Romanus.
And in other manuscripts:
"to Romanus his son-in-law, the husband of his daughter."
And in the year 417
[417] of the Arabs, severe cold occurred in Baghdad in winter,
and the shores of the Euphrates and the Tigris froze,
and the date-palm trees were ruined.
And over the small canals people crossed on the ice (frozen crusts) in Baghdad.
And the farmers were unable to sow.
And in the same year, a decree went out in Egypt
that no one should kill an ox that draws a plow.
And a year later,
at the new moon of the first Rabi',
severe hail fell in Baghdad, like hens' eggs.
And in the year 1341
[1341] of the Greeks,
(1030 of our Lord? which is the year 421
Aleppo.
And the small force of Arabs who were in Aleppo
met the Romans and defeated them,
and killed many of them,
and the Arabs gained from the Romans an abundance of horses and weapons.
For the kings who were before Romanus,
because they refrained from persecuting the orthodox (believers),
were successful everywhere.
But this one who began to persecute,
and cast the holy Patriarch Bar 'Abdun and the bishops into exile,
and returned to the old custom,
the Lord also began to break the deceitful Romans before their enemies.
And in that same year,
when King Romanus heard that the Romans were defeated near Aleppo,
he gathered a great army, more than one hundred thousand,
and came to Antioch.
And from there he set out to advance against Aleppo.
And when two chiefs of the Slavs, with the force that was with them, had advanced a little ahead of the Roman army,
there encountered them about one hundred Ma'addite horsemen and a thousand foot soldiers;
and the Slavs were broken,
and turned their faces to flee.
And they brought news to the Romans,
"Behold, a force beyond numbering of Egyptians and Ma'addites are coming!"
And panic fell upon the Romans,
and King Romanus and his armies barely fled to Antioch, one horse at a time, without a battle
and without a blow.
And the Arabs overtook them,
and took from the Romans seventy camels with their baggage.
